newsitem.title: CHINA: Strong aftershock shakes northwest China region.
newsitem.headline: Strong aftershock shakes northwest China region.

text.p: An aftershock measuring 5.1 on the Richter scale shook China's remote northwestern region of Xinjiang late on Thursday, but there were no reports of any casualties, a seismological official said on Friday.
The aftershock, which struck at 9:37 p.m. (1337 GMT) on Thursday, had its epicentre at 35.4 degrees north, 78.2 degrees east in Xinjiang's Karakorum mountains, the official said.
The aftershock hit the same area as an earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale that rocked the mountainous area on Tuesday, the official said.
Tuesday's tremor caused no serious damage or casualties in the sparsely populated area, he added. "It took place in the mountains ... and was not very serious. Very few houses have cracks."
Chinese experts say the country is experiencing a period of intense seismological activity that will last until the end of the century.
A total of 50 earthquakes measuring more than 5.0 on the Richter scale hit China in 1995, an increase of 18.5 percent from the year before, official figures show.
